\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{مقررات} (moqarrarât)}{مقررات (moqarrarât)}]{\fa{مقررات} (moqarrarât) — regulations, rules}

\label{lesson:FA-C404-moqarrarat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a bachelor's degree, then the Persian for a doctorate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{مقررات}}
\textbf{\fa{مقررات}} (\emph{moqarrarât}) — \textquotedblleft{}regulations, rules\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مقررات} \fa{این} \fa{ساختمان} \fa{خیلی} \fa{سخت} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{moqarrarât-e in sâkhtemân kheyli sakht ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The rules of this building are very strict.
\end{quote}

A plural noun with the Arabic ending \emph{-ât}; one rule is \emph{qâ'ede} or \emph{qânun}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{مقررات}} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{muqarrarāt} \textquotedblleft{}things decided, laid down\textquotedblright{}, from the same Arabic family as \emph{qarār} \textquotedblleft{}a settled decision\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{moqarrarât}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{moqarrarât}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{moqarrarât}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a bachelor's degree, then the Persian for a doctorate, then say \emph{moqarrarât} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ممنوع} (mamnu')}{ممنوع (mamnu')}]{\fa{ممنوع} (mamnu') — forbidden, prohibited}

\label{lesson:FA-C404-mamnu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a doctorate, then the Persian for regulations.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ممنوع}}
\textbf{\fa{ممنوع}} (\emph{mamnu'}) — \textquotedblleft{}forbidden, prohibited\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{سیگار} \fa{کشیدن} \fa{در} \fa{اتوبوس} \fa{ممنوع} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sigâr keshidan dar otobus mamnu' ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Smoking is forbidden on the bus.
\end{quote}

On signs: \emph{vorud mamnu'} — no entry.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{ممنوع}} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{mamnū'} \textquotedblleft{}prevented, forbidden\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a doctorate, then the Persian for regulations, then say \emph{mamnu'} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{مجاز} (mojâz)}{مجاز (mojâz)}]{\fa{مجاز} (mojâz) — allowed, permitted}

\label{lesson:FA-C404-mojaz}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for regulations, then the Persian for forbidden.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{مجاز}}
\textbf{\fa{مجاز}} (\emph{mojâz}) — \textquotedblleft{}allowed, permitted\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{استفاده} \fa{از} \fa{موبایل} \fa{در} \fa{کلاس} \fa{مجاز} \fa{نیست}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{estefâde az mobâyl dar kelâs mojâz nist.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Using mobile phones in class is not allowed.
\end{quote}

The opposite is \emph{gheyr-e mojâz}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{مجاز}} \textquotedblleft{}allowed\textquotedblright{} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{mujāz} \textquotedblleft{}permitted\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{رعایت} \fa{کردن} (re'âyat kardan)}{رعایت کردن (re'âyat kardan)}]{\fa{رعایت} \fa{کردن} (re'âyat kardan) — to observe, to comply with}

\label{lesson:FA-C404-reayat-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for forbidden, then the Persian for allowed.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{رعایت} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{رعایت} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{re'âyat kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to observe, to comply with\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{همه} \fa{باید} \fa{قوانین} \fa{را} \fa{رعایت} \fa{کنند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hame bâyad qavânin râ re'âyat konand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Everyone must obey the rules.
\end{quote}

\emph{Re'âyat} \textquotedblleft{}observance, care\textquotedblright{} + \emph{kardan}. For rules and laws, and for hygiene too.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{رعایت}} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{ri'āya} \textquotedblleft{}care, guarding, observance\textquotedblright{}; with \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} it means to keep a rule.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{re'âyat kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{re'âyat kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for forbidden, then the Persian for allowed, then say \emph{re'âyat kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{نقض} \fa{کردن} (naqz kardan)}{نقض کردن (naqz kardan)}]{\fa{نقض} \fa{کردن} (naqz kardan) — to break, to violate}

\label{lesson:FA-C404-naqz-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for allowed, then the Persian for to observe.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{نقض} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{نقض} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{naqz kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to break, to violate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{آن} \fa{شرکت} \fa{قانون} \fa{را} \fa{نقض} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ân sherkat qânun râ naqz kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
That company broke the law.
\end{quote}

For laws, rules and agreements; formal.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{نقض}} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{naqḍ} \textquotedblleft{}undoing, breaking\textquotedblright{}; Persian says the Arabic \emph{ḍ} as \emph{z}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
